candidate_relations.reason: The superficial bland single-layer vascular channels without atypia do not show the infiltrative kaposiform spindle-cell morphology expected for kaposiform hemangioendothelioma.
The biopsy lacks Kaposi sarcoma features such as spindle-cell fascicles, slit-like spaces, and hemosiderin, with Perls staining specifically negative.
Histology demonstrates a dermal vascular proliferation highlighted by CD31 and CD34 rather than basaloid epithelial nests of basal cell carcinoma.
The lesion consists of round endothelial-lined spaces in the upper dermis, not the storiform CD34-positive spindle-cell proliferation of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans.
Angioma broadly accommodates the CD31/CD34-positive vascular proliferation but does not identify the poikilodermatous plaque-like subtype shown by the atrophic violaceous plaque.
Neither the band-like endothelial channels nor the two-year atrophic calf plaque provides evidence of a destructive granulomatous process.
There is no chronic lymphedema or prior lymphatic disruption, and the endothelial cells are bland rather than malignant as required for Stewart-Treves syndrome.
Hemangioma captures the benign endothelial proliferation but omits the distinctive plaque-like poikilodermatous clinicopathologic form.
The plaque has an atrophic surface and upper-dermal band of vascular spaces rather than the hyperkeratotic epidermis and papillary-dermal ectasia of angiokeratoma.
A slowly enlarging 2-year erythematous-violaceous atrophic plaque on the calf is unlike the small bright-red dome-shaped papule of cherry hemangioma.
The biopsy is vascular with CD31-positive endothelial lining and does not describe the spindle-cell collagen trapping typical of dermatofibroma.
Single-layer endothelial cells without atypia in a nonindurated plaque conflict with the cytologic atypia and destructive growth of angiosarcoma.
No dermal small blue-cell tumor or neuroendocrine morphology is present; instead the specimen shows bland vascular channels.
The lesion is an atrophic plaque persisting for two years, not a rapidly growing friable polyp with lobular capillary architecture.
Round upper-dermal channels lined by flat bland endothelial cells do not show the plump epithelioid endothelial cells and inflammatory stroma of epithelioid hemangioma.
The chronic solitary plaque lacks neutrophilic inflammation, bacilli, and the immunosuppression context expected for bacillary angiomatosis.
CD31/CD34-positive endothelial channels establish vascular differentiation, while no basal-cell carcinoma component is reported.
Failure of topical corticosteroids and a biopsy dominated by endothelial vascular spaces argue against eczema.
Adult onset and gradual enlargement of a histologically proliferative dermal vascular plaque do not support a congenital structural vascular malformation.
The channels are lined by a single bland endothelial layer without the characteristic hobnail cells or hemosiderin of targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma.
